content.text:
I migrated `src/module.ts` to es-toolkit and wrote the result to `out/module.ts`. It passes type checking, but I could not compare its output against the original. Lodash isn't installed, so `src/module.ts` doesn't type-check or run here. I also had no size measurement for the original. The bundle is 1962 bytes (min+gzip), with 113 bytes of my own code. An earlier variant measured 1947 bytes, with 121 bytes of own code, but it had the `zipObject` import removed.

| lodash | es-toolkit | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `merge` | `merge` from `es-toolkit` | Same in-place mutation and return value. On a nested object/array patch (shorter array, partial objects, `null`) I checked it gives the same result as `es-toolkit/compat`, which is lodash-compatible. |
| `startCase` | `startCase` from `es-toolkit/compat` | The strict version differs on consecutive capitals: `USER2name` gives `User 2 Name` instead of `USER 2 Name`, and `XMLHttp2Go` gives `Xml Http 2 Go` instead of `XML Http 2 Go`. That is within your input range, so I used the compat one. |
| `fromPairs` | `zipObject` from `es-toolkit` | `fromPairs` exists only in compat. I used strict `zipObject(pairs.map(p => p[0]), pairs.map(p => p[1]))` as a small adapter. It was smaller than the compat `fromPairs` (2009 bytes, 85 bytes of own code). Duplicate keys keep the last value, as before. |

I didn't hand-write any replacements. The only extra code is the one-line adapter around `zipObject`.
